prize_parts.citation: For conceiving and demonstrating targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, using designed heterobifunctional molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have changed my configuration. In round 1 I proposed Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B007 alone. After reading the full exchange I now propose two parts: Crews and Deshaies for degraders, and Liu for base editing, three people in total. My first reason is that B007 stands on the concept. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders. That is the one claim all three B007 supporters share, and a citation that says 'designed heterobifunctional molecules that direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system' is accurate without Ciulli, Handa, Sakamoto or the glue strand. It is a priority statement I can defend, and it avoids a contested cut among eight names. Second, B061 is the cleanest case on the shortlist and the one I ranked third. It is molecular design in the sense I care most about: an engineered deaminase on a programmable scaffold, and an adenine deaminase evolved for a substrate no natural enzyme accepts. It changes what researchers and clinicians can do, since many labs use it routinely and first patients have been treated. Third, the two parts are different achievements, one acting on proteins and one on nucleic acids, each a chemical operation made programmable. I do not offer this pairing to produce consensus. I offer it because it is the configuration I can justify part by part, and because the chair's questions made me see that the Ciulli seat added design depth but not priority.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B007 remains timing, since no degrader has an approval yet, and I give this moderate weight because the principle is reproduced by independent groups and degraders are in late-stage trials. Dropping Ciulli removes the person whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made PROTACs a rational design discipline, and a critic can say the prize honours the idea and leaves out the people who made it drug-like. Handa's cereblon discovery is also left out of the citation, and the committee may find the glue strand too important to omit. For B061, the 2020 CRISPR prize is close, long-term safety is unsettled, and Nishida and Kondo reported cytidine-deaminase base editing at essentially the same time. A two-part prize may also be criticised as a bridge between first choices rather than one idea.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes Crews and Deshaies for B007 with Liu for B061, as two distinct achievements acting on proteins and nucleic acids, and stops the degrader part at the concept in order to leave room for a second part.
responses.response: I now move to your configuration, and I want to say why. In round 1 I held Ciulli for the third B007 seat. Your point that Crews and Deshaies hold the clearest priority for the concept, while the three-name cap forces an arbitrary choice between Ciulli and Handa, is persuasive. Leaving the third seat open and giving it to Liu is easier to defend than choosing between two real contributors. I do not share your reason that the two parts are a clean pair of mechanisms. For me the common thread is molecular design: choosing a target and recruiting a catalyst or an E3 ligase to act on it. I accept that this is a thread and not a single principle, and that it has to be argued, not assumed.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa with a citation that includes the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, arguing that Handa's identification of cereblon ties the PROTAC and glue strands into one principle.
responses.response: I still do not think cereblon belongs in the same citation. The PROTAC concept is a design principle that works with any E3 ligase and any binder. Cereblon explains how thalidomide and its analogues act, and that is a mechanism that was found, not designed. Writing both into one citation either weakens the unifying statement or implies Handa and Ito are Crews and Deshaies's co-discoverers, which the history does not support. I agree the glue strand is a real breakthrough and a future committee may want to recognise it separately. With three people available across the whole configuration, I would rather give the third seat to Liu than choose between Ciulli and Handa.

responses.point: Aqvist makes base editing his whole prize with Liu alone, and argues that it is a chemical transformation of a base and not a programmable nuclease, so it is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: Your argument on this point is the one that moved me. I had worried that B061 refines a platform already recognised in 2020. The adenine base editor required evolving a deaminase for a nucleoside no natural enzyme acts on, and that is protein and nucleobase chemistry in its own right, not a variation on Cas9 cleavage. I still share your maturity concern about off-target and bystander editing and long-term safety, and I do not think it is smaller than the degrader timing risk. But I no longer think the CRISPR proximity should keep B061 as an alternative. Where we differ is that I would keep B007 as a co-equal part, because degraders created a modality across many targets.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, pairs sequencing-by-synthesis (Balasubramanian and Klenerman) with Liu, framed as reading and rewriting DNA, and asks whether the committee wants a pair that has a convincing common principle.
responses.response: I agree that Liu belongs in the configuration and that a pair should not be justified only by shared first-choice votes. For B001, my round-1 doubts remain. The decisive step is shared between reversible-terminator chemistry, optics and instrumentation, DNA sequencing was recognised in 1980, and the Solexa and 454 credit split is not clean without Rothberg, Ju and Mayer. Reading and rewriting DNA is an attractive framing but it is a rhetorical link between a measurement method and an editing chemistry. Degraders and base editing are, in my view, closer in kind, since each makes a chemical operation programmable by a recognition element.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B007 premature this year, which I would weigh less if a first approval is imminent
Whether Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work is close enough to require crediting, which would break the three-person limit
Whether the committee accepts a Crews and Deshaies citation without Ciulli, Handa or Sakamoto as historically fair
Whether the pairing of B007 and B061 reads as a coherent prize or as a bridge between first choices
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no direct personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies or Liu or to any other shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey are not credited names. My peptide and lipid assembly interests overlap with Emma Sparr's and bear on B034 and B049, neither of which is in my preferred configuration.
